core_obligations: Choose local data (proof lines 7592-7596): for a point y of Y and each x in the fibre X_y pick a quasi-compact neighbourhood E_x of x inside an open U_x; since f is proper the fibre X_y is quasi-compact, so finitely many U_{x_1}, ..., U_{x_n} cover X_y.

Show the union of images is a neighbourhood (proof lines 7597-7603): let Z = f(X minus the union of the U_{x_i}); as f is closed, Z is closed, and it does not contain y because the U_{x_i} cover the fibre over y, so the complement of Z is an open neighbourhood of y.

Read off the covering condition (proof lines 7601-7603): since f is surjective, Y minus Z is contained in the union of the images f(E_{x_i}), which are quasi-compact, so the union is a neighbourhood of y covered by finitely many quasi-compact subsets, which is the qc covering condition.
proof_roadmap: Fix a point of the target and cover the quasi-compact fibre by finitely many opens with quasi-compact neighbourhoods.
Use closedness of the proper map to produce a closed set whose complement is a neighbourhood of the point.
Use surjectivity to place that neighbourhood inside finitely many images of quasi-compact sets.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a proper surjective morphism f : X -> Y of locally quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces is a qc covering (statement lines 7584-7589). The proof has one genuine topological move: after covering the quasi-compact fibre X_y by finitely many opens U_{x_i} equipped with quasi-compact neighbourhoods E_{x_i}, one uses closedness of f to make Z = f(X minus the union of the U_{x_i}) a closed subset avoiding y, and surjectivity to place the resulting neighbourhood of y inside the finite union of the images f(E_{x_i}) (proof lines 7592-7603). The non-formal content is the choice of Z and the two properties of proper maps used to control it. The claim is H2: one finite covering argument with a standard closedness input.
